A guide to fixing Access denied errors in the admin console

If the admin console answers with "Access denied", the cause is almost always one of four things: the account is missing the role the page requires, the session expired while the tab was idle, the request came from an address your organisation has not allowlisted, or a proxy in front of the console stripped the authentication header. This guide goes through each cause in turn and shows the exact screen where you can confirm it.

1. Check the role on the account

Open Settings, then Members, and read the Role column. A member with the Viewer role can open every page in the console except the ones that change billing or delete data; those answer with "Access denied" on purpose. If the person needs them, change the role to Editor and ask them to reload. The change takes effect immediately and does not require a new sign-in.

2. Check the session

A session that has been idle for more than eight hours is closed. The next request is answered with "Access denied" rather than a redirect, because the console cannot tell an expired cookie from a missing one. Signing in again in the same tab restores the page; nothing is lost because the form state is kept in local storage.

3. Check the allowlist

Requests from outside your office ranges are refused with "Access denied" and a Ray ID in the response header. Copy that Ray ID into the support form and support can tell you which rule refused the request. This is the same code Cloudflare reports as error 1020 when a WAF rule blocks a request, so the two screens look alike: read the heading, not just the words.

4. Check proxies and extensions

Some corporate proxies remove the Authorization header. The console then sees an anonymous request and answers "Access denied". Loading the console from a different network is the quickest way to tell this case apart from the others.

Still stuck?

Send the Ray ID, the page address and the time of the request to support. Please do not paste your password or a session cookie into a ticket; support never needs either of them to look at a refusal, and a ticket is the last place they should be written down.
